credibility.line: No promise has come due yet in this window

threads.title: Store opening count scaling and targets
threads.note: Last mentioned Aug 2024; not repeated on the 2 calls since

history.speaker: Neville Noronha
history.quote: If you were to look at our store opening trend, we do 40-something stores, but in another two to three years, this 40 should go to a 60 or a 70 per year.

history.speaker: Neville Noronha
history.quote: So you can take a range of 40 to 60 over the next three years.

threads.title: Annual store opening target for FY25
threads.note: Last mentioned Jul 2024; not repeated on the 3 calls since

history.speaker: Neville Noronha
history.quote: We are primed and ready in terms of opening around 40-50 stores. I mean anything between that is what we are ready and we will deliver broadly. Obviously subject to regulation, permission, all of that, but we have that kind of inventory to at least commit saying 40-45, we will do, every year.

threads.title: GMA contribution trend for FY25
threads.note: Last mentioned Aug 2024; not repeated on the 2 calls since

history.speaker: Neville Noronha
history.quote: With a reasonable confidence, I can say that, this financial year will be equal to or better than FY '24 GMA contribution.

history.speaker: Neville Noronha
history.quote: With a reasonable confidence, I can say that, this financial year will be equal to or better than FY '24 GMA contribution.

threads.title: Gross margin guidance range medium term
threads.note: Last mentioned Aug 2024; not repeated on the 2 calls since

history.speaker: Neville Noronha
history.quote: I keep saying this. I don't know what is the aspiration level in the analyst community on gross margin, but we've been towering between 14% and 15%, or 14% and 15.5%, and that's where it's going to be.

threads.title: Store expansion acceleration and annual rate
threads.note: No reported number to check this against

history.speaker: Neville Noronha
history.quote: We have opened 50 stores last year and we hope to continue the acceleration and actually try and open as many more than we have opened in the past.

history.speaker: Neville Noronha
history.quote: Like we have always said that the right method of expansion in the offline space is to open on an average every year at least 10% to 15% or maybe 10% to 20% of your base stores – every year.

history.speaker: Anshul Asawa
history.quote: I do want to state that internally, our benchmarks will remain that we should be opening around 15% of our store base as the number that we want to increase annually.

threads.title: General Merchandise and Apparel contribution medium term
threads.note: No reported number to check this against

history.speaker: Neville Noronha
history.quote: It's a drop, but more or less it's coming back. But just to pre-empt some of the questions that may come on this, we are not going to be 28% or 27% like it used to be earlier. A broad trend line will be around the current run rates of around 23%, is the sense we get.

history.speaker: Anshul Asawa
history.quote: I think we've been maintaining for the last few years that we expect this particular part of the business to be somewhere in that 22% to 23% kind of a range.

history.speaker: Neville Noronha
history.quote: But broadly, we feel that this is a business that can be broken even in a couple of years. So that's broadly what we feel about this.

threads.title: DMart Ready store count next year
threads.note: No reported number to check this against

history.speaker: Neville Noronha
history.quote: I mean, it won't be less than 50. I mean, if you're talking so much about it.

threads.title: Net profit margin North Star long term
threads.note: No reported number to check this against

history.speaker: Anshul Asawa
history.quote: And a net margin also, we believe that if we can be around that 5% type of a range, ballpark range, we are quite happy with that. So I don't see any significant material impact that should happen on the net margin front.

threads.title: Borrowing target for FY27

history.speaker: Niladri Deb
history.quote: So we might go to an INR2,000 crores borrowing by the end of the year, but that is all going towards managing capex.

business.what: Avenue Supermarts Limited operates retail supermarkets and e-commerce grocery delivery, providing everyday low prices through everyday low-cost operations and physical store expansion.

segments.note: Online grocery business focused on 11 key cities

business.quote: The model that this business has of providing everyday low price through an everyday low-cost operation isn't just a strategy, but it also has become its moat and will continue to protect us for years to come.
